title: Adobe MAX Sneaks 2026: ten AI prototypes that point to Photoshop and Premiere
summary: Adobe demonstrates ten AI prototype features for Photoshop and Premiere at MAX Sneaks 2026
detailed: Adobe showcased ten AI-based research prototypes at MAX Sneaks 2026, including video tools like Scene Sweep and Live Set, and image tools like Deep Brush and Hands On.
The prototypes focus on maintaining creative workflows within familiar environments like Photoshop and Premiere.
For the first time, Adobe opened a Labs Playground to allow users to test prototypes and provide feedback before considering their integration into official product menus.
sentences: Adobe has showcased ten AI-based research projects at MAX Sneaks 2026 that anticipate the direction of its creative tools.

In video, Scene Sweep stands out, which propagates an editing decision across all shots in a sequence, and Live Set, for reframing and transforming in real time, alongside On Cue, which controls the exact moment of a generated action.
These are laboratory promises, not release dates.

In the realm of image, Deep Brush adapts brushstrokes to shape, color and lighting, while Hands On allows elements to be manipulated with controls directly on the canvas and Link Up returns editable vectors after processing.
The technical proposal is about maintaining the creative's workflow without taking them out of their usual environment.
For the first time, Adobe opens a Labs Playground to test some prototypes and gather feedback from users before deciding their future integration into Photoshop and Premiere.
Ten prototypes that edit for you, guess the exact moment and return vectors to you as if nothing.
Of course, they all live in the laboratory, that place where features are wonderful until they reach the real menu and ask for a separate subscription.
For now, it's time to try them in the Playground and give your opinion, which is free.
We'll see how many survive the journey from the demo video to the toolbar.
